basis: Inherited keratan-sulfate sulfation defect causes corneal deposits, stromal opacification and visual loss; a metabolic disorder need not cause systemic injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective keratan-sulfate sulfation is an inborn glycosaminoglycan metabolic disorder, despite predominantly ocular injury.

basis: Storage disease defined by skeletal and cardiac involvement; neurologic deterioration 30-79%. Cap omits common airway dysfunction, hearing loss and retinal degeneration.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac involvement is explicitly defining; abnormal heart morphology occurs in 80-99%, with valve abnormalities in 30-79%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal abnormalities define the disease; dysostosis multiplex occurs in 99/126 and limited joint mobility in 80-99%.

basis: Inherited hepatobiliary metabolic disorder with cholestasis and periportal fibrosis; diarrhea and bleeding do not establish direct intestinal or blood-organ injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: chronic diarrhea in 1/1 reported patient does not establish direct intestinal damage; secondary effects of cholestasis are insufficient.

basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment and hypomyelination define disease; visual impairment is cerebral. Single-case cardiac and skeletal annotations do not establish prevalence of at least 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: individual cardiac defects have single-case annotations in a cohort of at least four; involvement in at least 30% is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: hip and foot abnormalities have single-case annotations; neither major diagnostic status nor prevalence of at least 30% is established.

basis: Acute CNS and cardiovascular sympathomimetic poisoning; hypertension occurs in 30-79%. Infarction, pulmonary injury, seizures and renal injury are minority complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiovascular sympathomimetic toxicity defines the poisoning syndrome, including hypertension in 30-79%; infarction is not required.
decisions.neurologic: primary: acute central nervous system toxicity defines this poisoning, distinct from a purely psychiatric cocaine-use disorder.

basis: Central autonomic respiratory-control failure defines disease. Hypoventilation does not establish intrinsic lung injury; Hirschsprung disease (~16-30%) is separately diagnosed.

decisions.pulmonary: none: ventilatory failure originates in central autonomic control; intrinsic lung or airway damage is not established.

basis: Inherited oxysterol metabolic disorder; progressive spastic paraplegia is the predominant presentation (>50% of reported cases). Hepatic disease characterizes a much rarer subtype.

decisions.neurologic: involved: progressive corticospinal degeneration in spastic paraplegia is the predominant CYP7B1 phenotype (>50%), rather than a rare subtype complication.

basis: Autoimmune encephalitis; direct antibody-mediated enteric dysfunction causes persistent severe diarrhea and weight loss in approximately 50-70%.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct enteric autoimmunity causes sustained intestinal loss of function, with severe diarrhea and weight loss in approximately 50-70%; tissue destruction is not required.

basis: Lysosomal disorder defined by skeletal disease and developmental impairment in most; visual impairment 80-99%. Single-case cardiac annotations do not establish common involvement.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay and intellectual disability in most patients are explicitly included among the disease's defining features.

basis: Short-rib skeletal dysplasia; stage 5 kidney disease in 2/2 patients. Narrow chest does not establish lung injury; hepatic cysts in 1/2 lack documented functional impairment.

decisions.pulmonary: none: narrow thorax alone does not establish pulmonary hypoplasia or sustained lung dysfunction in at least 30% of this specific subtype.
